title: Investigation of Dipole-Stabilized Skyrmions in Amorphous Centrosymmetric FeGdPt Multilayers using 4D-STEM
content: Magnetic skyrmions are most commonly stabilized by a Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction (DMI) in magnetic materials with noncentrosymmetric crystal structure. However, skyrmions can also form due to the competition between the long-range dipolar and short-range exchange energy interactions in centrosymmetric crystal structures [1]. These dipole-stabilized skyrmions exhibit a unique three-dimensional (3D) structure with Bloch-type domain walls and Néel-type caps at the surfaces [2]. Here, we study the formation of these dipolar skyrmions in a thin film of sputtered amorphous FeGdPt multilayers [1] using four-dimensional scanning transmission electron microscopy (4D-STEM). Unlike Lorentz TEM, 4D-STEM allows for the capture of the full convergent-beam electron-diffraction (CBED) pattern at each probe position. This simultaneously provides information about the internal magnetization field and the amorphous grain structure of the profiled material. We use 4D-STEM to investigate magnetic phase changes and their underlying grain structure under applied perpendicular magnetic fields to unravel how microstructure plays a role in the formation of dipole skyrmions in centrosymmetric magnets.
